steps.text: most of us thank other people all day. when was the last thank-you turned inward?
not for big wins. for the quiet things: getting up, trying again, being decent when it was hard.

steps.reply: thanks, given and received. kept in the book.

options.label: nice
options.reply: it is. the thanks we give others belongs here too.

options.label: odd
options.reply: it often is, the first few times. gratitude usually points outward. this is a new direction.

options.label: hard to take
options.reply: that's honest. let it sit there anyway. no need to accept it fully yet.

ideas: trying, even when it was hard.

steps.text: gratitude practices tend to lift well-being a little. thanking yourself is a newer idea, built on the same habit of noticing what's good.
steps.evidence: emerging (small effects; thanking yourself is less studied)

steps.text: before sleep, give one quiet thanks for something done today.

grounding.idea: gratitude interventions show small effects on well-being
grounding.source: Davis et al., 2016, Journal of Counseling Psychology
